title: Sparkling Water 12-pack

drivers.name: Store closed Monday for renovation
drivers.evidence: One weekday closure reduces potential sales by ~14% (1/7 of week). Historical data shows similar closures reduce sales by ~12-15% when measured. No other drivers present.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 95.0. The store is closed Monday, reducing the week's selling days by 1/7. No promotions, events, or price changes are active. The classical uplift model suggests no adjustment, but the planner note about closure is a named driver. A store closure on a weekday typically reduces weekly sales by ~12-15% (based on 1/7 day loss and partial demand transfer). The noise-adjusted effect is credible and consistent with prior closures. No post-promotion dip is expected. The median is adjusted downward by 14%, with modest downside spread to reflect uncertainty in closure impact.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-39% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
